rationale: The exact-commit normal-build FastAPI comparison on Linux x86-64 qualified five matched asyncio repetitions and four matched uvloop repetitions. Rust delivered 0.652x and 0.726x of Uvicorn throughput while using 1.96x and 1.75x server CPU per request. The broader three-system category evidence also shows repeated HTTP/1.1 and WebSocket regressions. The Python ASGI compatibility path therefore does not meet the original faster-than-Uvicorn objective. Retain compatibility and correctness gates for Python ASGI; target the performance claim at the Python-free Rust-native application path. The release verifier must still validate a complete exact-commit matrix before accepting a candidate.

scope.comparison: stock FastAPI and Starlette under uvicorn-rs-py versus Uvicorn

scope_revision.statement: Treat uvicorn-rs-py as the optional Python ASGI compatibility server, without a performance superiority claim over Uvicorn. Target server performance claims at Python-free Rust-native application composition; keep Python ASGI parity and benchmark results as compatibility and regression evidence.
scope_revision.rationale: The normal-build validated-route run used a bodyless GET, so request-body copying cannot explain its measured regression. Instrumented stage data points to extra Python ASGI wall time and task scheduling but does not establish a causal function-level attribution. Further Python-boundary work should be justified by a correctness-preserving before/after measurement rather than the original general speed objective.
